purpose: Document how external public datasets can support evaluation credibility as references, while clarifying that they do not directly replace the project-specific golden labels.

amazon_reviews.relevance_to_project: Useful for product review language, rating-based sentiment reference, product category metadata, and review schema design.
limitations: review data is not the same as customer complaint email data
does not naturally provide store location or source attribution labels
not a direct replacement for the current golden labels

cfpb_consumer_complaints.source_type: official U.S. government financial consumer complaint database
cfpb_consumer_complaints.relevance_to_project: Useful for complaint issue taxonomy, consumer narrative style, product/issue/sub-issue structure, and public complaint analytics reference.
recommended_use: possible auxiliary benchmark only after domain caveats
limitations: financial services domain rather than retail product email domain
not a statistical sample of consumers' marketplace experiences
consumer narratives are consumers' own descriptions and are not necessarily verified facts
not direct ground truth for this project

bitext_customer_support.source_type: customer support intent and response dataset
bitext_customer_support.relevance_to_project: Useful for customer support intents, category design, entity/slot reference, and response wording examples.
recommended_use: optional auxiliary sanity set after mapping
limitations: not aligned to full current schema
not a direct replacement for internal golden labels

customer_support_ticket_datasets.source_type: public or sample support ticket datasets
customer_support_ticket_datasets.relevance_to_project: Useful for support ticket metadata, priority/status workflow, issue category design, and channel handling.
recommended_use: optional external validation set after license and schema review
limitations: may not be official authoritative benchmarks

next_stage_recommendation: Proceed to I-3.6 golden label candidate review before expanding to larger synthetic data.
